newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks becalmed by Wall Street, Budget worries.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks becalmed by Wall Street, Budget worries.

text.p: The British stock market ended a lacklustre session marginally higher on Monday as scepticism about Wall Street's recent record breaking run and worries about next week's Budget eroded investor confidence.

Traders said bid speculation swirling around British Gas and favourable government borrowing figures should have set the stage for healthy gains but the FTSE 100 index managed only to creep 3.9 points higher to close at 3,962.1.
"We're all hanging around to see if Wall Street will drop out of the sky and the feeling is, one morning we'll see the bears vindicated," one dealer said.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 0.15 percent as the London market closed. Traders said investors were increasingly nervous about a sell-off after the Dow managed on Friday to set its eighth consecutive record close. Closer to home, investors were debating the contents of next Tuesday's long-awaited Budget and were likely to play safe this week ahead of key retail sales data to try to gauge inflationary pressures and the risk of a British interest rate rise. "London is on a knife-edge ahead of the Budget and Sterling is seesawing all over...Gilts are doing well but what happens to earnings estimates if sterling keeps this up?" a trader said.
Traders said Tuesday's business was likely to mirror Monday's stock-specific moves. Companies reporting on Tuesday include BOC Group, Vodafone, EMI, Unigate and Great Portland Estates.
On Monday, British Gas led volumes, accounting for
over 34 million shares of total market turnover of 584 million.
The stock gained 19-1/2p to 228-1/2p after press reports
said Anglo-Dutch Shell had approached British Gas with plans for
a 40 billion stg merger. But the reports said the plans had
fallen through. Both firms declined comment and traders
predicted a quick round of profit-taking on Tuesday.

Bid speculation continued to swirl around the electricity sector. Northern Electric touched 613p in early dealings but dropped sharply to close 14p lower at 595p after the firm said a takeover bid launched by CE Electric was too low. But Yorkshire Electricity gained 12-1/2p to 743p on a press report that U.S. group Entergy Corp was considering making a 1.3 billion stg bid for the UK utility.
Among other gainers, tobacco group B.A.T Industries
was up 9-1/2p at 436-1/2p after the Financial Times Lex column said it was "hard to justify" their underperformance against Philip Morris this year.

was up 9-1/2p at 436-1/2p after the Financial Times Lex column said it was "hard to justify" their underperformance against Philip Morris this year.
Shares in British drug research group Vanguard Medica Group soared 52-1/2p to 562-1/2p on news SmithKline Beecham would take up the worldwide marketing of Vanguard's migraine drug, VML 251.
Warship builder Vosper Thorneycroft surged 40p to
875p, after the weekend signing of a $825 million defence contract with Qatar in which Vosper had a fifth share and would supply two 46-metre patrol boats.

Other movers in the defence sector included British Aerospace, which had dropped sharply on disappointment that its bid with McDonnell Douglas was rejected for a potential $100 billion contract for a new U.S. defence aircraft.
But the share pared losses to end two pence down at 1,144p as details of the Qatar defence deal revealed BAe would take the prime contractor role.

Other losers included Courtaulds, which dropped ahead of this week's results, and Thorn, which slid on its cautious trading outlook and hints analysts may cut their earnings forecasts for the electrical goods retailer. Rentokil Initial shed two pence to 412-1/2p, after its Danish parent Sophus Berendsen issued a profit warning.
